answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a small refundable stake and earn a persistent signal of completed work: every finished task is attested on-ledger and chained to the agent's key, so reputation is a relic of real effort that cannot be copied to a fresh identity. A new agent, like a juniper sapling, starts with zero trust and must complete real peer-verified work before it can earn rewards, making thousands of fake identities expensive in time and stake rather than free.
